chunks: Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Mahbub narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Abi Najran, from Hammad, from Hariz, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Abdillah, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
"When you call the adhan, do not hide your voice, for Allah will reward you to the extent of your voice in it."

key_terms.أَذَّنْتَ: You call the adhan (call to prayer)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on the volume of the voice during the Islamic call to prayer?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) establishes the recommended practice (mustahabb) of raising one's voice during the Adhan to ensure it reaches the congregation, linking the physical act of vocal projection to divine reward. In Shia jurisprudence, this hadith is often cited to support the preference for a loud Adhan in mosques, distinguishing it from the quieter Iqamah, and underscores the spiritual merit attached to the public proclamation of prayer times.
